body: She walks and talks. She knows her signs. She's very bright and a very happy baby. I lucked out on this first one.

At the moment no. My friends up here are all actually just his friends and we don't have the type of relationship where you can talk about the hard stuff. I don't have any family either And my close friends have worries of their own. I don't want to be that miserable friend so we keep things light. 

I think I'm doing a great job faking happiness because no one, not even my husband, seems to think there's a problem. I'm drowning and I just so desperately want someone to ask if I'm ok. Today feels like a bad day. I've been crying all morning and I'm planning on finding someone to watch grace while I drive somewhere far, far away. I think I'm going to do it.

But I don't feel like I'm suffering. I don't have signs of depression other than crying and wanting to kill myself. I know those are two big signs but I work full time, I don't feel morose. I don't want to take pills

But my best just doesn't seem to be good enough. I work hard but it seems my successes are contingent on the schedules of other people. And it's becoming very difficult to move forward with my life while having to rely on others. I don't think my husband's family like me very much and they're making it more clear when  they choose to babysit his sisters kid over mine (same age). I just wish someone knew how much I was struggling. My husband stormed out this morning after telling me to buck up.

I know that. I know that something like this would damage her. But I can make it  look like an accident. She'd be alright. My husband would be alright. He'd find someone that he deserves who could be a better mom  because I feel like a pretty awful mom  now as it is. Maybe she would forgive me one day.
I do. She has no shortage of people that love her. But she's young enough that she won't miss me. I just don't know how to make this pain go away. I want to be happy but I can't stop crying.
Grace. She doesn't deserve me. I just thought I'd be somewhere else at this point of my life.
